mainTopic: Building the מקדש with non-holy materials: the leftover incense and רב פפא's reason
overview: The גמרא challenges the view that the בית המקדש building is first built with חול materials and made holy only afterward. It quotes a משנה from שקלים: leftover incense was redeemed onto the artisans' wages, given to them, and bought back with new-year money. If the building starts out חול, why not redeem the incense onto the building? The גמרא answers that the building work was not worth as much as the incense. It then asks why that matters, since שמואל says הקדש can be redeemed onto something worth only a פרוטה. The answer is that שמואל's rule works only בדיעבד, not לכתחלה. רב פפא then explains why the מקדש is built with חול materials: workers might sit or lean on the materials, and that would be מעילה if they were holy. A משנה about logs that are subject to מעילה seems to contradict him. He answers that the משנה is about logs meant for use that same day. The chapter ולד חטאת then ends.

steps.title: Quoting the משנה about leftover incense
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a משנה describing how the Temple dealt with leftover incense: it was redeemed onto the artisans' wages, given to them, and bought back with new funds.
steps.simpleTranslation: They raised an objection: What did they do with the leftover incense? They set aside from it the amount of the artisans' wages. They redeemed it onto money owed to the artisans, gave it to the artisans, and then bought it back with money from the new collection.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is quoting a משנה as the source for a challenge. This step sets up the question that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Leftover incense from last year had to be treated as if it were bought with this year's funds. So the Temple moved its holiness onto the artisans' wages, paid the artisans with the incense, and bought it back with new money. The procedure itself is the clue the גמרא will use to attack.

keyTerms.meaning: The incense left over from the previous year
The wages of the artisans who worked in the בית המקדש
They redeem, moving the holiness off an item onto something else
The new collection of שקלים for the new year

phrases.english: They raised an objection:
phrases.notes: The source quoted here is a משנה in שקלים, chapter 4.

phrases.english: The leftover incense
what would they do with it?
They would set aside from it
the wages of the artisans.
And they would desacralize it
onto the money of the artisans,
and they would give it to the artisans,
and they would go back and take it
from the new collection.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a challenge against the view from the earlier discussion that the building is built from non-holy materials and consecrated afterward.
steps.kashyaTarget: The view that the Temple building is first built from non-holy materials (בונין בחול ואחר כך מקדישין)
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The source is quoted here; the actual attack comes in the next step.

steps.title: Why not redeem the incense onto the building?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why such a long procedure was needed when the incense could have been redeemed onto the non-holy building.
steps.simpleTranslation: But why? Let them redeem it onto the building!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא sharpens the challenge. If the building starts out non-holy, it could take on the incense's holiness, so the artisans' wages would not be needed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to the view that the building is built non-holy and consecrated afterward, the finished building is a perfect place to put holiness. The incense's holiness could move onto the building, and then the incense would be free. The משנה's choice of the wages suggests that this option did not exist.

keyTerms.meaning: Why?
Let him redeem it (move its holiness off)
The building, construction work in the Temple

phrases.english: But why?
Let them desacralize it onto the building!
phrases.notes: Meaning the non-holy building would take on the incense's holiness.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the challenge out of the משנה quoted in step 1.
steps.kashyaTarget: The view that the building is built non-holy and consecrated afterward
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the building can receive holiness, the משנה should have redeemed the incense onto it. Using the wages instead implies the building cannot receive holiness this way.

steps.title: There was no building project
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the משנה speaks of a time when no construction was happening.
steps.simpleTranslation: It speaks of a case where there is no building.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends the view by limiting the משנה to a time with no construction going on.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If nothing was being built, there was nothing to redeem the incense onto. So the משנה does not prove the building cannot take on holiness. It only shows that no building was available.

keyTerms.meaning: Where there is not

phrases.english: Where there is no building.

steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the case (אוקימתא) to a time without construction
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה seemed to show that the building cannot be used for redemption.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה speaks when no construction was taking place, so there was no building available.

steps.title: But the משנה mentions artisans
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the answer: the משנה speaks of artisans' wages, so building work must have been going on.
steps.simpleTranslation: But it teaches 'the money of the artisans'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the answer from step 3 using the wording of the משנה itself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Artisans are paid for work, and in the Temple that means construction. So it is hard to say there was no building project when the משנה talks about artisans' wages.

keyTerms.meaning: But surely (introduces a difficulty)
It teaches (in the source)

phrases.english: But "the money of the artisans"
it teaches!

steps.kashyaTarget: The answer that there was no building
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה mentions artisans' wages, which shows construction was happening.

steps.title: The building was not worth enough
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that there was construction, but not enough to equal the value of the leftover incense.
steps.simpleTranslation: It speaks of a case where there is no building equal to the amount of the money.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא refines its answer. There was building work, but it was too small to take on all the incense's value.
steps.deeperAnalysis: To redeem something, you need an item worth at least as much. The construction was smaller than the value of the incense, so they could not redeem onto it and used the artisans' wages instead. The view that the building starts out non-holy survives the challenge.

keyTerms.meaning: Equal to the amount of
Where there is not

phrases.english: Where there is no building
equal to the amount of the money.
phrases.notes: The money here is the value of the leftover incense.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 4 by refining the answer of step 3.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Refined limitation of the case: construction existed but was too small in value
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Either there was no construction at all, or the building should have been used.
steps.terutzMaskana: Construction existed, but its value was less than the incense, so redemption onto it was not possible.

steps.title: Can't you redeem expensive הקדש onto something cheap?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges step 5 using שמואל's rule that הקדש worth a מנה, redeemed onto something worth only a פרוטה, is validly redeemed.
steps.simpleTranslation: But doesn't שמואל say that if הקדש worth a מנה was redeemed onto something worth only a פרוטה, it is redeemed?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the last answer. Even if the building work was worth less than the incense, why not redeem the incense onto it anyway?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 5 said the construction wasn't worth enough to cover the incense. But שמואל holds that הקדש can be redeemed onto something worth far less than itself. So a small amount of construction should be enough, and the long procedure still seems unnecessary.

keyTerms.meaning: Property that belongs to the בית המקדש (holy property)
A large sum: one hundred דינרים
The smallest coin that has legal value
He redeemed it / it is redeemed: the holiness moves off the item

phrases.english: But doesn't Shmuel say:
Consecrated property worth a maneh (one hundred dinars)
that one redeemed onto something worth only a peruta, it is redeemed!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer of step 5 that the construction was not worth enough
steps.kashyaTarget: Step 5's claim that the construction's low value prevented redeeming the incense onto it
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: According to שמואל, the value of the item you redeem onto doesn't need to match the הקדש, so low-value construction should still work

steps.title: שמואל's rule only works after the fact
steps.stepSummary: שמואל's rule applies only בדיעבד; the גזבר should not plan to redeem הקדש for less than its value לכתחלה.
steps.simpleTranslation: That applies only if someone already did it; at the outset, one should not.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that שמואל was only talking about after the fact. A גזבר may not set out to redeem something valuable onto something cheap.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The difference is between בדיעבד and לכתחלה. The redemption counts if it was done, but the מקדש's treasurers would not choose this path from the start. So the long procedure in the משנה is the proper way, which keeps the answer of step 5 standing.

keyTerms.meaning: These words apply (only) to... — limits the scope of a rule
Where one already did it (after the fact, בְּדִיעֲבַד)
At the outset, as a plan of action

steps.whatToRemember: Redeeming הקדש for far less than its value works only בדיעבד, not לכתחלה. That is why the משנה's longer procedure was needed.

phrases.english: This applies where one already did it,
but at the outset, no.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 6 by limiting שמואל's rule
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the scope of the cited rule (בדיעבד vs. לכתחלה)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: שמואל's rule lets you redeem large הקדש onto small value, so small construction should be enough
steps.terutzMaskana: שמואל's rule only works after the fact; at the outset you need value that matches, so the משנה's procedure was needed

steps.title: Why the מקדש was built with non-holy materials
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא explains that the builders used חול materials because workers are human and might lean or sit on the stones, which would be מעילה if they were holy.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said: This is why they build with חול materials. The תורה was not given to ministering angels. Perhaps a worker will want to rest and will sit on the materials. If he builds with holy materials, he will end up committing מעילה.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא gives the reason behind the practice of building the מקדש with חול materials and making them holy only afterward. This connects to the idea in step 2 of redeeming onto the building.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Workers get tired and lean or sit on what they are working with. If the stones were already הקדש, that personal use would be מעילה. So the materials stay חול during construction and become holy only once the building is finished.

keyTerms.meaning: Non-holy, ordinary
The תורה was not given to ministering angels: its laws are made for real people with human needs
To lean or sit down to rest
Making personal use of holy property

steps.whyThisMatters: This explains why the building could be a non-holy item at all (the idea used in step 2), and it sets up the next challenge.

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said: This is the reason
that we build with non-sacred materials:
the Torah was not given to the ministering angels.
They said: perhaps he will want to lean and rest,
and he will lean on them.
phrases.notes: "Them" means the building materials, like the stones.

phrases.english: If he builds with consecrated material,
it turns out that he is misusing consecrated property.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב פָּפָּא אָמַר: הַיְינוּ טַעְמָא דְּבוֹנִין בַּחוֹל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the reason behind the practice of building with חול, which was assumed in step 2
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The מקדש is built with חול materials so that workers who lean or sit on them do not commit מעילה

steps.title: The משנה about the logs bought by the treasurers
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes a משנה: when the גזברין bought logs, one is liable for מעילה on the logs, but not on the sawdust or the leaves.
steps.simpleTranslation: We learned: if the treasurers bought logs, one is liable for מעילה on them, but not on the sawdust or the leaves.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a משנה to set up a challenge against רב פפא. The actual question comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה shows that the logs were holy while still being worked, since מעילה applies to them. Only the leftover bits, the sawdust and leaves, are free of מעילה. This seems to clash with רב פפא's idea that building materials stay חול during the work.

keyTerms.meaning: The treasurers of the בית המקדש
One is liable for מעילה
Sawdust or shavings from cutting wood
Leaves or twigs that fall off the log

phrases.english: We learned: the treasurers who bought logs,
one is liable for misusing them,
but one is not liable for misusing the sawdust
nor the leaves.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a source that will be used to challenge רב פפא
steps.kashyaTarget: רב פפא's reason for building with חול
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Setup: the משנה shows wood being worked on was holy and subject to מעילה

steps.title: Why weren't the logs left חול too?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks: according to רב פפא, the logs should also have stayed חול while being worked on, so why does the משנה treat them as holy?
steps.simpleTranslation: But why is one liable for them? Here too, let him work with חול wood. After all, they said perhaps he will want to rest and will lean on them, and he will end up committing מעילה with holy items!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא presses the challenge. רב פפא's worry about workers leaning should apply to logs just as much as to stones.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If workers might sit on stones, they might just as easily sit on logs. So by רב פפא's reasoning the logs should have stayed חול until they were set in place. Yet the משנה says מעילה applies to them, which means they were already holy.

keyTerms.meaning: Why? — introduces a challenge
Here too — applying the same logic to a new case
It turns out, it will be found

phrases.english: But why is one liable for misusing them?
Here too, let him work with non-sacred wood,
since they said that perhaps he will want to lean and rest,
and he will lean on them,
and it turns out that he is misusing consecrated items!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאַמַּאי מוֹעֲלִין בָּהֶן? הָכָא נָמֵי לֶיעְבַּד בַּחוֹל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the משנה from step 9 to challenge רב פפא's reason in step 8
steps.kashyaTarget: רב פפא's reason that building materials stay חול so workers won't commit מעילה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The same worry applies to logs, yet the משנה treats the logs as holy during the work, which contradicts רב פפא's principle

steps.title: Logs for later use stay unholy, but the משנה is about logs used the same day
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא answers that his rule fits logs bought for future use. The משנה is talking about logs bought to be used that same day, so they can be holy right away.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said: If we were talking about logs bought for use from now on (over a longer time), then yes, they should stay חול. But when the משנה taught that there is מעילה on the logs, it meant logs to be used that same day.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא answers the challenge against his own rule by showing that the משנה is talking about a different kind of case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: His rule was that materials stay חול because workers may sit or lean on them while they wait to be used. That worry only applies to logs that will sit around for a while. Logs bought to be used the same day go straight into the work, so no one will lean on them, and they can be holy right away.

keyTerms.meaning: Logs or wood
From now on, meaning for use later on over time
Yes, indeed, that is correct
Of that day, meant for use the same day

steps.whatToRemember: Building materials for later use stay חול, so workers will not commit מעילה by leaning on them. Materials meant for use that same day can be holy right away, because there is no time for that problem to come up.
steps.confusionAlert: רב פפא is not taking back his rule. He agrees that logs for later use stay חול. He is only saying the משנה is talking about a different case.

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said:
If it were about logs for use from here on,
indeed so (they would stay unholy).
But when we learned in the Mishnah (that there is misuse),
it was about logs for that same day.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי בְּעֵצִים דְּמִכָּאן וְאֵילָךְ, הָכִי נָמֵי. אֶלָּא כִּי תְּנַן בְּמַתְנִיתִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 10 by narrowing the case the משנה is talking about.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the cases: logs for later use versus logs for the same day
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה's logs seemed to go against רב פפא's rule that building materials stay חול.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה is talking about logs used the same day, where the worry about workers leaning on them does not apply, so they can be holy right away.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Logs for later use stay חול; logs bought for use that same day are holy, and there is מעילה on them.

steps.title: Hadran: closing the chapter of ולד חטאת
steps.stepSummary: The chapter called ולד חטאת ends here.
steps.simpleTranslation: We will return to you, chapter ולד חטאת.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the traditional closing line that marks the end of the chapter.
steps.deeperAnalysis: It is not part of the argument. It is a farewell to the chapter we just finished, along with a promise to come back and learn it again.

keyTerms.meaning: We will return to you, the line said when finishing a chapter
The name of this chapter, taken from its opening words

phrases.english: We will return to you, "The offspring of a sin-offering"

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Marks the end of the chapter after the last back-and-forth is settled.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The chapter ולד חטאת is finished.
